## CEO overview

- **What is changing:** Firstmate now waits for each worker's own expected pause before telling the captain that worker is stuck, instead of using one short timer for everyone.
- **Why it matters:** Some workers routinely pause for a couple of minutes while they check in or claim work. Those healthy pauses were looking like stalls and paging the captain.
- **Customer or business impact:** The captain gets fewer false stuck-worker alerts during normal Grok waiting cycles and Pi branch claims, while real stalls and dead watchers still page.
- **Risk and rollout:** Low. The parent still only watches worker records and does not change how workers take or finish work. Work a live actor has already claimed stays with that actor. Dead leftover claims cannot hide a stall.

## What changed technically

- Parent stall paging uses each local secondmate's recorded wake cadence plus a short grace, instead of a fixed 60-second wait. Grok background-notify waits use 180 seconds; Pi branch claims use 300 seconds; other mates stay at 60 seconds. A whole-threshold override remains available.
- Unclaimed-row detection reads recorded harness and live branch-grant state, never pane text. Live claimed rows stay with the actor. Dead grants cannot hide an over-window row. A stale watcher beacon pages immediately.
- Architecture, configuration, and scripts docs match the cadence-aware path. Executable regressions cover healthy Grok and Pi waits, over-cadence paging, stale beacons, live claims, dead grants, and lease isolation.
- An optional one-line parent note of routine branch verdicts was left unimplemented because stall observation must stay read-only of the mate home, and writing that note would itself create a wake. Pi already shows those notes on the captain conversation.

## Validation

- **Checks passed:** Hosted product checks on this head all pass: lint, coverage, four portable serial shards, two portable parallel shards, Herdr, stock macOS Bash snapshot, repository invariants, timing aggregate, and Require no-mistakes. Locally, the wake-queue suite and operator checkpoints cover healthy Grok waits, over-window paging, stale beacons, live Pi claims, dead grants, and lease isolation.
- **Checks not run:** No live multi-hour fleet soak. The operator checkpoint uses deterministic fixtures rather than waiting out real production cycles.
- **Evidence and limitations:** Parent observation is read-only of mate homes; foreign queues stayed byte-stable in every checkpoint. The [operator checkpoint transcript](https://github.com/bingb0t5/firstmate/blob/2e832791b7d82edee69d887d1dd64c093c44595b/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-pi-branch-stall-mirror-r1/stall-detector-demo/transcript.txt) records quiet Grok 175s and Pi 274s waits, paging past cadence plus grace or on a stale beacon, a live Pi claim staying quiet, and a dead grant still paging.

## Module-boundary decision

Current module retained: stall paging stays in the parent watcher, which already observes local secondmate queues without locking or rewriting them. Cadence and live-claim skip use recorded supervision state in the mate home rather than a new detector or pane-text guessing.

## Decision needed

No decision required.
